beyond_this_chapter.finding: Nothing in this chapter changes how an earlier chapter should read.
beyond_this_chapter.why: The notes here concern tempo, idiom and the decline vocabulary in section IV only; the retained terms 'wine worm', 'threshing ground' and 'mu' are used as established, and no identity or term is corrected by this passage.

changes.find: showed its effect on the spot
changes.reason: 覿面に現れた is immediate effect; 'took effect at once' says that in plain English idiom without weakening the cure's completeness, which the crux requires.

changes.find: This year is the third since he spat out the wine worm
changes.reason: 今年で、酒虫を吐いてから、三年になる is a plain statement of elapsed time; 'This is the third year since' is the English idiom for it.
changes.replace: This is the third year since he spat out the wine worm

changes.find: the round and sleek fullness of former years
changes.reason: 丸丸と肥つてゐた俤 is simply the roundly fat figure of former years; 'sleek' and 'fullness' ennoble and expand it, and the reading requires Liu's fatness to stay plain and verbally stable as the counterpoint to his decline.
changes.replace: the round fat figure of former years

changes.find: Skin of a poor lustre hangs greasily over the bones of a gaunt face
changes.reason: 色光沢の悪い皮膚が、脂じみたまま、険しい顔の骨を包んで: the skin wraps (包んで), it does not hang, and 険しい is stern/harsh, not thin; 'dull, greasy' keeps R3's readability gain without adding the looseness or thinness the Japanese gives elsewhere or not at all.
changes.replace: Dull, greasy skin wraps the bones of a stern face

changes.find: only a little hair, touched with frost, lingers upon his temples
changes.reason: 霜に侵された双髩が、纔に、顳顬の上に、残つてゐるばかり is hair barely remaining on the temples; 'remains' keeps that plain sense in idiomatic English where 'lingers' prettifies it.
changes.replace: only a little frost-touched hair remains on his temples

changes.find: how many times in a year he takes to his bed
changes.reason: 一年の中に、何度、床につくか、わからない位 needs the ordinary English measure 'how many times a year'; the hearsay ださう is already carried by 'they say'.
changes.replace: how many times a year he takes to his bed

changes.reason: とんとん拍子に傾いて is brisk, successive decline, not steady gradual sinking; 'in quick succession' restores the tempo and its almost comic rapidity, in the smallest form rather than F1's 'tumbled', which adds a manner the Japanese does not specify.
changes.replace: has gone downhill in quick succession

changes.find: now of the suburban fields counted at three hundred mu, most have passed into other hands
changes.reason: 三百畝を以て数へた負郭の田も、多くは人の手に渡つた: 負郭 is fields around the town walls, and 'suburban fields counted at' misleads and reads as an inventory label; the replacement keeps 'mu' as the draft's retained term and puts the measure in English order.
changes.replace: now most of the three hundred mu of fields around the town have passed into other hands

changes.find: has willy-nilly taken hoe in unpractised hands, and passes his wretched day-to-day existence
changes.reason: 余儀なく is compulsion, which modern 'willy-nilly' no longer says, and その日その日を送つてゐる is living out his days; 'has been forced to take up the hoe' and 'drags out his wretched day-to-day life' match both the Japanese sense and English idiom.
changes.replace: has been forced to take up the hoe with unpractised hands, and drags out his wretched day-to-day life

changes.find: In fact this question has been repeated by people of every trade living in Chozan, and answered from the mouths of those same people in every kind of way.
changes.reason: 現にこの疑問は、長山に住んでゐる、あらゆる職業の人人によつて繰返され、且、それらの人人の口から、あらゆる種類の答を与へられた is the narrator's amused report of local gossip; the active form restores that light voice the reading requires, where the passive committee phrasing sags and slips number ('this question' for two questions).
changes.replace: In fact people of every trade in Chozan have asked it again and again, and answered it themselves in every conceivable way.

changes.find: Liu must before long have died, without question
changes.reason: もし酒虫を除かなかつたなら、劉は必久しからずして、死んだのに相違ない is counterfactual, not inference about a past death; 'would before long have certainly died' states the second answer's argument in correct English, without strengthening or weakening its certainty.
changes.replace: Liu would before long have certainly died

changes.find: Liu from of old did nothing but drink.
changes.reason: 劉は、昔から酒ばかり飲んでゐた is plain statement, not pastiche; the replacement keeps it blunt so the bald equation that follows stays bald, as the crux requires.
changes.replace: Liu had all his life done nothing but drink.

changes.find: If wine were taken from Liu's life, nothing would remain behind.
changes.reason: 劉の一生から酒を除けば、後には、何も残らない: 'remain behind' is redundant padding that dulls the sentence on which the third answer's equation rests; the sharper conditional keeps exactly the Japanese claim and nothing softer.
changes.replace: Take wine from Liu's life and nothing would remain.

changes.find: then it is entirely natural that the health and fortune of the Liu of former days should have been lost
changes.reason: 失はれたのも、至極、当然な話であらう: dropping the doubled hedge 'then…should have been' lets the third answer land, while keeping 'entirely' for 至極 rather than R9's 'only natural', which would soften the force of the conclusion.
changes.replace: it is entirely natural that the health and fortune of the Liu of former days should be lost

declined.reason: Declined in part: its suggested 'round, sleek fatness' retains 'sleek', which F3 correctly identifies as an addition to 丸丸と肥つてゐた; the counting idiom in R2 is taken (see changes), but the fatness wording follows F3 and the reading's requirement that Liu's fatness stay plain and stable.

Declined in part: its suggested 'hangs loose over the bones of his gaunt face' and 'still clings to his temples' contradict the Japanese — 包んで is wraps, not hangs loose (looseness is an inference the text leaves to the lost fat), 険しい is stern, not gaunt (F2), and hair 残つてゐる is remaining, not clinging; the readability core of R3 (dull greasy skin, natural word order) is taken in plainer form.

disagreements.faithful_side: F3: 丸丸と肥つてゐた is simply roundly fat; 'sleek' is ennoblement/expansion with no basis in the sentence.
disagreements.readable_side: R2: keep 'the round, sleek fatness of former days' while fixing the year-counting.

disagreements.choice: F2 on the adjective and the verb: 'stern face', skin 'wraps' the bones; R3 taken only for 'dull, greasy' and natural order.
disagreements.faithful_side: F2: 険しい means stern/harsh, not thin, and the skin 包んで (wraps) the bones; 'gaunt' and 'hangs' interpret rather than translate.
disagreements.readable_side: R3: the sentence is dictionary English with wrong verbs; rewrite as 'Skin dull and greasy hangs loose over the bones of his gaunt face…hair still clings to his temples'.

data.say: Changes and declined notes are recorded above; two reader disagreements (p53, on 'sleek' and on 'gaunt/hangs loose') are settled by the reading in favour of the faithful reader and do not go up; nothing is sent to the editor, and no earlier chapter is affected.
